pattern-selector.why: the design was chosen on purpose: a separate per-task receipt plus a shared grounding-primitives module, rejecting both overloading the PR receipt and copying the grounding logic.
pattern-selector.what: chose one task-receipt CLI (write/check/export) over an append-only per-session store, with receipt-grounding.mjs as the single owner of the grounding primitives; recorded the options and the rejected ones in ADR-0097.
quotes: the structure that fits the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

architectural-decision-records.why: the decision (a per-task receipt outside a repo, tied to file hashes, with shared grounding primitives) is recorded in the same change.
architectural-decision-records.what: added docs/adr/0097-per-task-receipts-hash-tied.md (context, three considered options, decision, consequences with honest limits), section 11 of the receipt spec, and a CHANGELOG entry.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the seven issue behaviors (files-outside-change, selection mismatch, non-verbatim quote, stale/copied, parallel sessions, empty, 400-file full check) are enumerated as scenarios, stored, logged, and run on the harness.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: appended seven @audience:agent scenarios to the two always-on feature files with step defs driving the real task-receipt.mjs, refactored the shared end-its-turn step into a dispatcher, regenerated the datastore, and appended the coverage log.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the receipt behaviors are proven at the lowest layer that can catch the bug: unit/integration tests that spawn the real CLI.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: added test/task-receipt.test.mjs covering the accept path, every refusal (empty, stale, uncovered, ungrounded, hash-mismatch, files-outside-change, selection, expired waiver, traversal, directory-as-file, malformed), the per-session store, and export.
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the per-task checker is itself a check, so it must be proven able to fail: its tests flip when the checker is neutralized.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: test/task-receipt.test.mjs is discriminating: against a no-op check (always exit 0) every refusal test flips and the positive test's 'accepted' assertion fails; the refactor of the PR gate is pinned by its existing 27 passing tests.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

skeptical-audit.why: the receipt enforces evidence in code - grounded quotes and current file hashes, refusing a stale, copied, or empty receipt - and the ADR carries evidence states and named limits.
skeptical-audit.what: the checker refuses any receipt that is not grounded against the installed skill text and the current file hashes; the ADR and spec name the limits (caller-supplied changed-list; completeness disclosed without a selection; the finish hook must itself fail closed).
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: the checker parses an untrusted receipt and resolves an installed skill file from a receipt-supplied name, so it is threat-modeled against path traversal and injection.
owasp-secure-coding-bdd.what: skill and session names are rejected if they are '.'/'..' or carry path separators before any join, the resolved skill file is realpath-contained inside the skills dir (matching the PR gate), input is parsed as JSON never eval'd, and the file read is hashed never executed; covered by test/task-receipt.test.mjs.
quotes: Each per-sheet file states the real attack the control stops

judge-arch.why: a fresh-context review ran on the diff before this receipt; it raised four findings (two medium, two low), all fixed and pinned, and is recorded in the arch-review log.
judge-arch.what: dispatched the four-questions review to a general-purpose subagent; fixed the '..' traversal, the silent completeness downgrade, the overclaimed 'one place' extraction, and the dropped waiver approver/expires, plus the unwrapped hash read; recorded in docs/arch-reviews/log.jsonl.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no new system or data architecture, schema, service, or scaling surface; the boundary, ownership, and error-handling review for this receipt tooling is carried by judge-arch (applied) and the design by pattern-selector (applied).

arch-encode.why: no new greppable arch-gate rule was encoded; the enforcement is a runtime fail-closed checker plus discriminating tests, not a static lint over source.

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, release, rollout, cutover, migration, or feature flag; nothing about what runs in production changes.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service, endpoint, SLO, alert, or on-call surface; local CLI tooling invoked by an agent or a future finish-check hook.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: the per-task store holds task metadata (ids, file paths, hashes, skill quotes), not personal or regulated data; it is local, append-only tooling output with no consent, retention, or deletion duty.

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no UI; command-line tooling with no rendered interface.

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser- or device-facing code; Node CLI scripts.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no user-facing UI; the CLI's developer-facing messages name the cause and the fix, following the repo's existing checker-message style.
